title: Signal-Aware Calibration and Verification Harness for Hybrid FP8/INT8 Profiles
creator: Aisha Karim
description: Create an automated harness that validates calibration profiles for mixed FP8/INT8 rollouts using signal-aware cohorting, probabilistic gating, and multi-metric pass/fail logic. The harness should enable deterministic replays, seedable adversarial perturbations, and per-cohort thresholds so quant rollouts can be gated automatically or flagged for manual review.
background: We've seen several regressions during quant rollouts caused by edge cohorts (long-context code completions, multi-turn dialogues, and instruction-heavy prompts). Existing golden-based checks are necessary but insufficient: they treat all prompts equally. This ticket builds a harness that weights signals (context length, domain category, model confidence, token-entropy) and computes cohort-level metrics to produce more actionable gates.
objectives: Design a signal schema for per-request weighting (context_length, response_length, confidence, token_entropy, user_domain)
Implement calibration replay runner supporting FP8/INT8 candidate binaries and baseline FP32 reference
Compute multi-metric suite: embedding cosine delta, log-prob KL, output edit-distance, ROUGE-L span fidelity, and end-to-end task accuracy when applicable
Provide configurable pass/fail gates per cohort with hysteresis and tiered severity (block, warn, review)
Integrate with CI (PR gate) and Console (dashboard + trace links) with stable artifact storage for audits
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a full suite against 10k anchors + 50 adversarial perturbations in under 4 hours on CI infra
Per-cohort report generated with metrics and a recommended gate decision (pass/warn/block)
Automatic posting of results to PR with artifacts link and concise summary
Configurable thresholds stored in runtime-2.4 config and feature-flag controlled rollouts
End-to-end test demonstrating a blocked rollout when a synthetic cohort exceeds tolerance on embedding-delta and log-prob KL
design_notes: We will use a two-stage scoring pipeline: (1) per-sample metrics + signal-derived weight -> normalized score; (2) cohort aggregation using weighted percentiles and uncertainty intervals (bootstrap). Metrics chosen to balance lexical and semantic drift: token log-prob KL (sensitive to fluency/regression), embedding cosine delta (semantic shifts), and edit-distance normalized by reference length (surface differences). For task-specific cohorts (code, summarization), we will enable task accuracy metrics and use monotonic gating rules.
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit per-sample metrics: embedding_cosine_delta, kl_divergence_logprob, normalized_edit_distance, rouge_l, response_latency_ms, model_confidence_score. Cohort-level: weighted_median, 90pct_upper, bootstrap_ci_95, pass_rate. Telemetry tags: run_id, model_candidate, baseline_model, quant_profile, hw_target, dataset_cohort.
gating_logic: Gate decision = evaluate metrics in order: (A) critical metric (embedding_cosine_delta) > cohort_threshold -> BLOCK; (B) if critical metric in warn band but combined score (normalized sum of standardized metrics) > warning_threshold -> WARN; (C) else PASS. Hysteresis: require two consecutive failing runs before auto-blocking production. Allow manual override with documented reason. For canary flows, use softer thresholds and require manual approval for block.
test_plan: Unit tests for metric computations, integration tests for replay runner with synthetic binaries, end-to-end CI job that runs on a small anchor set (200 queries) for PR-level fast-check, nightly full-run job for release candidates. Adversarial perturbation catalog maintained in repo (append-only) with provenance. Benchmarks to validate runtime: local runner, CI cluster, and dedicated GPU pool.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: land harness with PR integration and small anchor set (fast-check). Phase 2: enable nightly full-run with barrier flag disabled (results visible but non-blocking). Phase 3: enable canary auto-gating for behind-feature-flag customers on runtime-2.4. Phase 4: enable full auto-blocking for internal staging only, review after 2 weeks of stability.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed comparing bootstrap vs. analytic CI for weighted percentiles — bootstrap chosen for better robustness on skewed cohorts (A. Karim)
2026-03-04: PoC runner that replays saved request traces against candidate quant binaries and collects log-probs and embeddings (M. Liu)
2026-03-06: Defined metric thresholds for three initial cohorts (short-instruction, code-completion, multi-turn-chat) based on historical FP8/INT8 regressions — doc linked
2026-03-09: Integration PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-harness/pull/178 — unit tests passing on CI; exploring perf optimizations for embedding computation
open_issues: Performance: embedding extraction dominates runtime; investigate fp16 batch pipeline (ENG-?)
Cohort labeling: need resilient automated cohort extractor for incoming datasets; current labeling is manual
Adversarial catalog coverage: expand to include long-code snippets and multi-file prompts
risks: False positives during early runs could block healthy rollouts; to mitigate we default to WARN and require two failing runs for BLOCK. Embedding drift is sensitive to encoder updates; tests must pin reference encoder. CI runtime cost for nightly full-runs may be significant; propose using sampling and prioritized cohorts to control cost.
decisions: Use embedding cosine delta + log-prob KL as primary signals (chosen 2026-03-02)
Bootstrap-based cohort uncertainty preferred over analytic variance (2026-03-02)
Hysteresis: require two consecutive failing runs before auto-blocking production (2026-03-05)
